subject: Post-demo follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing, SDK auth & routing
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@lumendocs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: dedicated capacity sizing, SDK auth & routing

Thanks again for taking the demo call earlier, Sophie — appreciate the walkthrough of LumenDocs' ingestion/QA workflow. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we can align Engineering and Procurement: 

1) Primary integration points we heard:
 - SDK-based inference calls from ingestion pipeline (Python service).
 - Embeddings + reranker for candidate document retrieval.
 - Occasional tool-calling for metadata extraction (structured outputs).

2) Dedicated capacity asks / initial sizing:
 - Baseline: ~25 qps sustained (20 token avg per request) during business hours;
 - Peak bursts up to ~120 qps for batch digest windows (30–45m), with requirement for <150ms p50 on shorter prompts;
 - Need predictable per-token cost for budgeting (monthly committed capacity).

3) Integration/SDK questions we should cover next:
 - Auth: support for customer-managed API keys vs. token-exchange (we heard preference for irrevocable API keys behind KMS).
 - Routing: prefer region-anchored routing (us-west primary) with auto-fallback to us-east if capacity constrained.
 - Structured output: guarantee on top-level JSON schema + tool-calling hooks for post-processing.

Next steps (action owners):
 - Redwood: produce a short dedicated-capacity sizing proposal + example SDK auth pattern (Diego, Marissa) — target EOD Thu (2/19).
 - LumenDocs: send SOC2 questionnaire and any firewall/networking constraints (Sophie) — target EOD Thu (2/19).
 - Technical deep-dive: schedule 60m with Redwood Solutions Engineer to validate concurrency/queueing model (Marissa to propose times).

Attachments: I'll drop an initial sizing template in the shared Drive.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: dedicated capacity sizing, SDK auth & routing

Thanks, Diego — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our infra team after the call: 

1) Auth: We prefer customer-managed API keys that can be rotated via our KMS. Are there short-lived token exchange options for ephemeral hosts (Lambda-style workers)? We want to avoid long-lived secrets where possible.

2) Batching & concurrency: Our ingestion pipeline currently fans out to 40 concurrent workers during digest windows; each worker may make multiple in-flight requests. Curious how Redwood's queuing would handle 40 workers x up to 3 concurrent calls (120 concurrent inflight) vs. the continuous 25 qps baseline.

3) Embeddings/reranker: We plan to compute embeddings offline for the index (daily job) and use reranker for candidate re-scoring per-query. What's the recommended routing to reduce cross-region latency for embeddings lookup?

I'll upload the SOC2 questionnaire to you now (attached). Also, available for the deep-dive tomorrow (2/19) between 9–11am PT.

— Sophie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@lumendocs.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: dedicated capacity sizing, SDK auth & routing

Thanks Sophie — uploaded. Diego & I sketched a starting proposal and I attached a one-page sizing + policy doc (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf). Highlights and answers inline: 

Auth patterns
- Customer-managed API keys (recommended): Redwood supports customer-owned API keys stored in your KMS; keys are used for persistent services.
- Short-lived token exchange: we support a token-exchange flow (OAuth2-like) where services obtain ephemeral tokens (recommended for serverless workers). We can provide a lightweight token broker example in the SDK (Python + Node).

Routing & region failover
- Primary routing can be pinned to us-west with automatic fallback rules to us-east once queued latency would exceed SLO.
- For embeddings lookups we recommend colocating the embedding index in a read replica in the same region as the query tier; Redwood's routing layer can prefer local model shards to reduce cross-region RTT.

Queueing & concurrency model
- Dedicated capacity is sized in throughput units; each unit has concurrent token processing slots. For your pattern:
  - Baseline 25 qps sustained => recommend 6 capacity units.
  - Peak 120 qps bursts => enable burst pool (pre-warmed) + autoscale policy to add 3–4 units during digest windows.
  - Concurrency: Redwood enforces per-VM concurrency limits; we can configure per-route concurrency limit (e.g., 4 per worker) and provide a client-side retry/backoff sample to keep p50 targets.

Next steps
- Diego & Evelyn: can run the technical deep-dive tomorrow 2/19 at 09:30 PT — does that work, Sophie?
- We'll include an SDK sample for token-exchange and an example routing policy JSON in the Drive link.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf
